title: Cap. II Sol. Arg. 7 close: hortations keep elect persevering — scripture proofs of foresight-election end
pass_a_gloss: Last: as for the formula of the words themselves, Augustine rightly says (On Rebuke and Grace, ch. 13) that these things are said to the saints who will persevere as if it were held uncertain that they will persevere: for they ought not to hear it otherwise, for whom it is expedient not to be high-minded but to fear. Such exhortations are therefore applied to the elect themselves, not because their predestination is uncertain or hangs on the mutability of their will, but because by this means of exhortations, and by others which God knows to be apt, he brings it about that they persevere in grace and holiness. And these are the chief testimonies of the Scriptures which are brought to prove election from foresight of merits. If any others occur, it will be ready to take their true sense from these which have been explained. From testimonies, therefore, let us come to the adversaries' reasons.
pass_b_english: Last, on the wording itself: Augustine (On Rebuke and Grace 13) says these lines are spoken to saints who will persevere as if their perseverance were unsure — they need to hear it that way, not to be proud but to fear. So the elect get such warnings not because their predestination is shaky or hangs on free will's change, but because by exhortation and other means God knows fit, he makes them persevere in grace and holiness. Those are the main Scripture proofs used for election from foresight of merits. Any further texts take their sense from these. From the texts, then, to the adversaries' reasons.
source_text: Postremo, quod attinet ad ipsorum verborum formulam, recte Augustinus, De corrept. & grat. cap. 13. Perseveraturis sanctis sic ista dicuntur, quasi eos perseveraturos habeatur incertum: non aliter enim hoc audire debent, quibus expedit non altum sapere, sed timere. Hujusmodi ergo hortationes ipsis electis adhibentur, non quod incerta sit illorum praedestinatio, aut ex mutabilitate arbitrii illorum pendula, sed quod hoc medio hortationum, aliisque quae Deus apta esse novit, efficiat ut in gratia & sanctitate perseverent. Atque haec praecipua testimonia Scripturarum sunt, quae ad probandam electionem ex praevisione meritorum afferuntur. Si quae alia occurrant, ex hisce quae explicata sunt veram illorum sententiam desumere in promptu erit. A testimoniis ergo ad rationes adversariorum veniamus.
